parameters.content:
## Set these two before running

**Glean Chat** node -> replace `YOUR-INSTANCE-be.glean.com` in the URL with your Glean backend.

**Resolve channel** node -> paste your Slack channel id into `SLACK_CHANNEL` at the top, or fill `ACCOUNT_CHANNELS` to route per account.

n8n Variables are a paid feature, so neither is required. Where they exist, `GLEAN_SERVER_URL`, `GONG_SLACK_CHANNEL` and `GONG_ACCOUNT_CHANNELS` override both.

Credentials: Glean Trigger (TRIGGERS), Glean Client (SEARCH + CHAT), Salesforce, Slack.

Docs: https://developers.glean.com/cookbook/gong-call-follow-up-n8n

preset.cachedResultName: New call with participant as me

nodes.name: Glean Trigger
nodes.notes: GONG_2 — a new call the trigger creator took part in. The node registers the trigger on activation and removes it on deactivation.

parameters.jsonBody:
={{ JSON.stringify({ saveChat: false, messages: [ { author: 'USER', fragments: [ { text: 'Summarise this sales call for the account record in four sentences or fewer. Use ONLY the retrieved company documents below and the call itself as evidence. State next steps and owners if they were agreed. Do not infer commitments, dates, or pricing that were not stated. Then, on a final line by itself, write ACCOUNT: followed by the customer organisation the call was with — the external company, never a person and never our own side. Write ACCOUNT: UNKNOWN if the evidence does not say. Otherwise write only the summary: no preamble, and no closing question or offer of further help.

Call: ' + $('Extract call').first().json.title + '
Link: ' + $('Extract call').first().json.viewUrl + '

Permission-aware Glean results:
' + JSON.stringify($('Search Glean for call context').all().map(i => i.json)) } ] } ] }) }}

nodes.name: Glean Chat
nodes.notes: An HTTP Request, not a node: the Glean n8n package ships a Trigger and a Search action, and no Chat node. Runs as the credential owner, so the summary can only cite what that user can see.

nodes.name: Salesforce: list accounts
nodes.notes: Narrow this with a WHERE clause once the flow is working. It is unfiltered here so the resolution step below is the only thing deciding which account matches.

nodes.name: Salesforce: log call
nodes.notes: Salesforce is written before Slack on purpose. The Slack message says the account was updated; posting first would let it say so when the write then fails.

nodes.name: Slack: heads-up
nodes.notes: Only ever the account's own channel. There is no default; an unmapped account stops at the node before this one.
